newsitem.title: USA: Romania should persist on NATO.
newsitem.headline: Romania should persist on NATO.

text.p: Romanians should not be disheartened by not being among the first new members to be admitted to the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation this month, Gen. John M. Shaliskashvili, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, said on Wednesday.
The Clinton administration has decided to support adding only Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic when NATO members meet in Madrid later this month.

Asked what he would say to the Romanian people, 90 percent of whom reportedly support joining NATO, Shaliskashvili said, "I would answer them not to lose heart, to keep working hard, and they will be surprised at how quickily they, too, will be considered for NATO membership."

The news conference followed his speech at closing ceremonies for a joint peacekeeping training exercise that combined troops from four NATO countries and 18 Eastern European nations. The training began on June 11.
During his speech, Shaliskashvili, citing his Georgian ancestry, his birth in Poland and youth in Germany, said he never expected to see so many countries training together for peace.

"Less than eight years ago, most of these nations stood at ready behind the Iron Curtain," he said. "This cooperative exercise shows how far we've come from preparing for war against each other to preparing for peace with each other."

Later he said, "Whether in Haiti or Bosnia, it is almost impossible to envision the United States working in peace-keeping on its own. So it's important to cast our net very wide, so we are not limited in who can work with us."
